chapter_theme: Songs at Thiruvalangadu (திருவாலங்காடு), where Siva danced with Kali: the poet confesses scheming women, the body as a nest of Death, the tattvas that make up the body, and Death's messenger with the noose, and asks for the feet, the supreme state and the gift of Tamil praise; one song, sung at Thiruvothur, confesses praising unworthy patrons and names Murugan as Sambandar.
structure_note: Women (673); the body and Death (674, 676); the tattvas of the body and the bond (675); the poet's trade of praise and Sambandar's miracles (677). Song 677 names Thiruvothur (திருவோத்தூர்), not Thiruvalangadu.

673.reading: The poet heaps abuse on women with poison-sharp eyes and scheming minds, makers of blame, whose breasts show nail-scratches, who feed men a ghoulish food, who are wanton singers and charmers falling on deluded lovers, and asks that before his ruined mind delights in them on moonlit terraces he be granted the feet that flowers honour. The praise names Murugan's chest garlanded with flowers where bees hum 'thanathana' like the Veda, the hero Guha who rides the ram, who played with Valli's shoulders in the millet field, at Thiruvalangadu where Nataraja, the Lord of the world, danced with Kali.
673.nuance: பேய் அமுது ஊணிடு may refer to the charge that courtesans feed men a love-philtre; the reading is a guess. தகர் ஏறு, riding the ram, is a rarer mount than the peacock. காளியொடு ஆடிய: the shrine's dance contest of Siva and Kali. Several compound epithets in the first half (கீலகலாவிகள், காளிமவீணிகள்) are hard to divide.

674.reading: In a world where people celebrate sons and gold as their firm support, the poet asks that before the life that lives in this mean nest of a body, packed with fierce Death, is taken, and before people say his thought of praising Murugan has gone and speak scorn, the deeds swelling in his heart leave him and Murugan give his feet and rule him. The praise names Vishnu, who held up the hill as an umbrella, guarded the calves and swallowed the world, as uncle, Murugan who went infatuated to Valli and said 'rule me', and the grace that gives a fearless heart to those who bow with love, linked to the dancer who danced at Alangadu for the gods' life.
674.nuance: புதல்வரும் ... பொன்தான் என்று: the false supports named are sons and gold. புன்கூடு, the mean nest, is the body; கூற்றம் பொதிதரு, Death is already packed inside it. The line on the Alangadu dancer and 'the fruit of the song' (பாட்டின் பயன்) is obscure; it may allude to a poet-saint's songs at the shrine.

675.reading: The poet lays out how the body is made: earth, water, wind, fire and sky joined, the new mind yoked, the ten senses and organs, the four inner instruments, and the paths, until the body comes, bearing a hundred deeds of becoming and its own understanding, with Pati and the bond (pasa) shown; he asks Murugan to drive him off this world of illusion, come and raise his servant, and show the supreme state. The praise names the dancer who dances so that sages may hear and see Siva-knowledge, Lakshmi's lord and Brahma praising, the peacock ride that saved earth and sky, the vel that defeated Sura with his mountain and struck the seven seas, and Murugan who honours the hunter girl's feet at Palayanur Alangadu.
675.nuance: The first half is a short tattva doctrine: the five elements, the ten பொறி-புலன், the four கருவிகள் (the inner instruments), and பசுபதி பாசம், the Lord and the bond, before the plea for பரகதி. சுவமதி and புகல்வழி நாலைந்து (perhaps twenty paths) are not clear. பழனையில் ஆலங்காடு names the shrine's village Palayanur.

676.reading: The poet asks that before the dark-bodied messenger sent by Death throws his noose, and son, uncle, grandmother and kin hear of it, and life departs with the mind confused, Murugan show his feet on earth, remove the old deeds and sins that brought the body's disease, guard him daily, and rule him with the command 'sing the supreme praise in expansive Tamil'. The praise names Murugan the son of the dancer with the moon on his head at Alangadu, who brought the elephant to win the hunter girl he longed for, and whose vel split Sura in two and ended the gods' distress.
676.nuance: விரிதமிழால் அம் கூர்த்த பரபுகழ் பாடு என்று ஆட்கொள்: the poet asks to be ruled by a command to sing, the song itself as the form of grace. நோய் பண்டு ஏற்ற பழவினை: disease is traced to old deeds. ஒருதனி வேழம் கூட்டி: the elephant that frightened Valli into Murugan's arms.

677.reading: The first half praises Murugan as the great one who lives without lack with his companions, the vel that burned dry Sura, the seven seas and seven hills, the fighting cock, the peacock, Valli of the hunters and Devayanai of heaven, and the poet asks whether he too must sing endless songs to sinners who do not know that Murugan guards as a companion. The praise names the little one who, with the holy word flowing with honeyed nectar and with the white holy ash, made the male palmyra bear fragrant fruit that fell to the ground and sent to the stake the Jains who read no Veda, wear only mats and pluck their hair, at Thiruvothur by the red river.
677.nuance: The plea is about the poet's trade: பாவிகள் பாலும் தொலையாப் பாடலை யானும் புகல்வேனோ, singing to unworthy patrons. The praise gives Murugan two of Sambandar's deeds: the male palmyra made to fruit at Thiruvothur (பனை காய்த்து ... பழமாய்ப் பார்மிசை வீழும்படி) and the impalement of the Jains; திருநீற்றால் அமராடும் may refer to his curing the Pandya with ash.

links.note: Both confess the poet's trade of singing to patrons who do not deserve it; 358 quotes the begging speech, 677 asks only whether he must go on giving endless songs to sinners blind to the Lord's protection.

The Kural says the embrace of deceiving women (மாய மகளிர் முயக்கு) is an afflicting spirit (அணங்கு) to those without discerning understanding. The song's women are illusion-and-song charmers (மயமாயங் கீதவிநோதிகள்) who fall on deluded lovers (மருளாருங் காதலர் மேல்விழு) and feed them a ghoul's food (பேயமுது). Both name the deception and place the danger in the lover's lack of discernment, the song turning the Kural's spirit into a ghoulish meal.

The Kural compares the bond of body and life to a bird flying off and leaving its nest alone (குடம்பை தனித்தொழிய). The song calls the body a mean nest (புன்கூடு) where the life dwells, with fierce Death already packed inside it (பொங்காவெங் கூற்றம் பொதிதரு), and asks for the feet before that life is taken. The nest image is shared; the song adds that Death lives in the nest from the start.

The song lays out the body's making from earth, water, wind, fire and sky, the ten senses and organs and the four inner instruments, showing Pati and the bond (பசுபதி பாசங் காட்டி), and then asks to be shown the supreme state (பரகதி). Tirumular says the Lord fashions the body and lays out the range from earth upward so that the bond of the soul may leave (பசுபாசம் நீங்கிட). Both treat the tattva-built body as the setting in which the bond is shown and loosened.

Tirumular says the Lord made him well so that he would render the Lord well in Tamil (தன்னைநன் றாகத் தமிழ்செய்யு மாறே). The poet, before Death's messenger throws the noose, asks to be ruled by the command 'sing the supreme praise in expansive Tamil' (விரிதமிழால் அம் கூர்த்த பரபுகழ் பாடு என்று ஆட்கொள்). Tirumular states his calling as already given; Arunagiri asks for it as the form his rescue should take.

source_issues: Song 677 is grouped under திருவாலங்காடு but names திருவோத்தூர் (Thiruvothur) on the சேய்நதி.
